title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: Joseph Matlock informed me that thou had a prospect of going to Baltimore Yearly Meeting next and had also in course of conversation mentioned my name respecting it. He also said thou laid the same before him, I mean his going along he added that you could not set off until after your monthly meeting which comes next fifth day. Now I have thought whether you could not be easy to go without minutes, seeing by staying to the monthly Meeting the seventh day meeting at Baltimore will be lost to us, and that does not look easy to me to give up at this time, if I am permitted to go. Therefore I feel free to propose meeting you at Hezekiah Hopkins’ Ferry on this side next fourth day morning about seven o’clock with a a creature to put to a wagon, provided the one that is to go on the other side is free of courage, for mine is not suitable to go with a dull or one or that is slack of courage. Now as I cannot tell whether you will incline to give up staying your Monthly Meeting or not I have thought it might be right for me to hear from you before the time of Setting off. Therefore propose a letter being sent to Hopkins Ferry on this side on first day evening, & I expect if nothing happens to prevent to call there in the morning of Second day by seven O’Clock. & if it would be more convenient to get it there in the morning before the proposed hour it will be equal to me–so that I do not miss of it–as I expect then to go to the city & not to return until next day. That if my going with you should like to fall through, I should have an opportunity of looking out for other company.

closer.salute: with love to thee and thine from thy friend–

postscript.p: I expect Joseph will see thee before these lines come to land & perhaps will say something of my son which appears now to be in a favorable way respecting the operation on his throat—
